steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up basic HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and add a basic HTML structure with nested elements that we'll style using descendant and child selectors.
steps.hint: Start by creating a simple HTML structure with parent and child elements - think of a main container with headings, paragraphs, and lists inside.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: Basic nested HTML structure */

Main Title

Some paragraph text.

  • List item 1
  • List item 2
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic HTML structure with nested elements ready for styling with CSS selectors.
successCriteria: HTML structure is created with at least one parent element containing multiple child elements
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the foundation with nested HTML elements. This structure will let us practice descendant and child selectors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some HTML elements, but make sure you have nested elements (parent containing children) for practicing descendant and child selectors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure isn't quite right. Create a parent element (like a div) with several child elements inside it (headings, paragraphs, lists).

steps.title: Style the container element with a background color
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that selects the container element and gives it a light gray background color.
steps.hint: Use an element selector for the container and set the background-color property.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create your HTML structure here */

/* Add your CSS rule for the container element here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The container element will have a visible light gray background when the page loads.
successCriteria: A CSS rule exists that selects the container element and sets a background-color property to a light gray value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a background color to the container, establishing a visual base for the page.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure you're selecting the container element and setting a background-color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container element doesn't have a background color yet. Try adding a CSS rule that selects it and sets background-color.

steps.title: Introduce descendant selector syntax
steps.instruction: Add a descendant selector that targets all paragraph elements inside the container element, regardless of nesting depth, and set their text color to blue.
steps.hint: Use a space between the container selector and the paragraph selector to create a descendant selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The descendant selector will be written and ready to style nested paragraphs when HTML structure is added later.
successCriteria: A descendant selector with 'container' and 'p' separated by a space is created, setting text color to blue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a descendant selector that will target all paragraphs inside the container element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using a space between the container selector and 'p' to create a descendant relationship.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember: descendant selectors use a space between selectors to target elements nested at any depth within a parent.

steps.title: Apply descendant selector to style nested paragraphs
steps.instruction: Add a descendant selector that targets all paragraph elements inside the container and sets their text color to dark blue.
steps.hint: Use the container class name followed by a space and then 'p' to create a descendant selector, then add a color property.
steps.expectedOutcome: All paragraphs inside the container element will have dark blue text color when the descendant selector is applied.
successCriteria: A descendant selector '.container p' is created with a 'color: darkblue;' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a descendant selector that styles all paragraphs inside the container.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your selector targets paragraphs inside the container and sets the text color to dark blue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The descendant selector wasn't implemented correctly. Remember to use '.container p' to target paragraphs inside the container.

steps.title: Introduce child selector syntax
steps.instruction: Write a CSS child selector that targets only direct children of a parent element using the > symbol.
steps.hint: The child selector uses the syntax 'parent > child' to select elements that are direct children of the parent.
steps.expectedOutcome: A child selector rule is added to the CSS file.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a child selector using the > symbol that targets direct children of a parent element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully written a child selector using the > symbol. This will only affect direct children of the specified parent element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the > symbol between the parent and child selectors.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look like a child selector. Remember to use the > symbol between the parent and child selectors.

steps.title: Apply child selector to style direct list items
steps.instruction: Write a CSS rule using the child selector (>) to style only the direct <li> items inside the <ul> element with the color 'crimson'.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'ul > li' to target only list items that are direct children of the unordered list.
steps.expectedOutcome: The direct list items inside the unordered list will appear in crimson color, while nested list items remain unaffected.
successCriteria: A CSS rule using the child selector (ul > li) is added with the color property set to 'crimson'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully applied the child selector to style only direct list items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure the selector uses the child combinator (>) and the color is set to 'crimson'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: the child selector should be 'ul > li' with the color property.

steps.title: Compare descendant vs child selector results
steps.instruction: Add a descendant selector that targets all <span> elements inside the .container element, and set their font-weight to bold.
steps.hint: Use the descendant selector syntax (space between selectors) to style all <span> elements that are descendants of .container, regardless of nesting depth.
steps.expectedOutcome: All <span> elements inside the .container element (including deeply nested ones) will have bold text.
successCriteria: A descendant selector .container span is added with font-weight: bold;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a descendant selector that styles all <span> elements within the .container. This demonstrates how descendant selectors affect elements at any nesting level.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the descendant selector syntax (space between .container and span) and setting font-weight to bold.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a descendant selector that targets all <span> elements inside .container elements and makes them bold.

steps.title: Combine descendant and child selectors in one rule
steps.instruction:
Write a CSS rule that uses both descendant and child selectors to target all elements that are direct children of

elements inside the .container element.
steps.hint:
Use the descendant selector to target

inside .container, then the child selector > to target direct children of those paragraphs.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS rule will style <strong> elements that are direct children of paragraphs within the .container element.
successCriteria: A CSS rule with .container p > strong selector is written with at least one style property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully combined descendant and child selectors to target specific nested elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using both descendant (.container p) and child (>) selectors together.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rule doesn't correctly combine descendant and child selectors. Review the syntax: ancestor descendant > child.

steps.title: Use descendant selector with class names
steps.instruction: Add a descendant selector that targets all elements with class 'highlight' that are inside the .container element, and set their background color to yellow.
steps.hint: Use the descendant selector syntax with a class selector: .container .highlight { ... }
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will include a descendant selector that styles elements with class 'highlight' inside .container with a yellow background.
successCriteria: A descendant selector .container .highlight exists and sets background-color to yellow.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a descendant selector that targets elements with class 'highlight' inside the container.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your selector uses .container .highlight and sets background-color to yellow.
steps.feedbackWrong: The descendant selector with class names isn't quite right. Check the syntax and property.

steps.title: Use child selector with multiple element types
steps.instruction:
Add a child selector rule that targets both direct

and

children inside the .container element.
steps.hint: Use the child selector syntax with a comma to separate multiple element types that share the same parent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will contain a child selector that styles both direct h2 and p children of the .container element with italic font style.
successCriteria: The child selector targets both h2 and p elements directly inside .container and applies the font-style: italic property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a child selector that targets multiple element types. This demonstrates how to apply the same style to different direct children of the same parent.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your selector uses the child combinator (>) and includes both h2 and p elements separated by a comma.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review child selector syntax. Remember to use the > symbol between parent and child, and separate multiple element types with commas.

steps.title: Create a complex nesting scenario
steps.instruction: Add a deeply nested HTML structure with multiple levels of elements to demonstrate descendant and child selector scope differences.
steps.hint: Create a div with class 'complex' containing nested divs, paragraphs, and lists to build a multi-level structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: A multi-level HTML structure is created with nested elements to demonstrate how descendant and child selectors work differently in deep nesting.
successCriteria: The HTML structure contains at least three levels of nesting with various element types (div, p, ul, li, span).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a complex nesting structure that will clearly show the difference between descendant and child selectors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some nesting, but try adding more levels and different element types to create a truly complex structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't show enough nesting levels or element variety to demonstrate selector scope differences effectively.

steps.title: Review and test all selector combinations
steps.instruction: Add a final CSS rule to test a descendant selector for spans within paragraphs in the complex nesting scenario.
steps.hint: Write a descendant selector that targets span elements inside p elements, using the syntax 'p span'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A descendant selector for spans within paragraphs is added, allowing you to test how descendant selectors work in complex nesting scenarios.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a descendant selector rule for 'p span' with at least one property (e.g., background-color).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a descendant selector for spans within paragraphs. This completes your testing of all selector combinations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've written a descendant selector that targets span elements inside p elements (like 'p span') with at least one CSS property.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. Try writing a descendant selector for spans inside paragraphs using the syntax 'p span' with a CSS property like background-color.
